headline: S&P 500 futures edge higher pre-market on the final trading day of Q2 2026, extending Monday's tech-led relief rally, as U.S.-Iran Doha talks resume and investors await today's JOLTS data and Nike's after-close earnings.
stance: Constructive but headline-sensitive. Monday's session closed the strongest quarter for equities in six years — the S&P 500 (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 7,440.43) and Nasdaq (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 25,820.14) both bounced sharply off last week's lows, driven by Mag-7 re-engagement and easing Strait of Hormuz tensions. Pre-market futures are modestly firmer (S&P ~+0.1%, Nasdaq ~+0.2%), but the macro backdrop is complex: the Fed under Chair Warsh has pivoted hawkish, core PCE is running at 3.4% — well above target — and markets are pricing three rate hikes this year with the first move likely in September. Any flare-up in Middle East talks or a hot JOLTS print could reprice that path quickly.

news.head: Iran ceasefire fragile; Doha talks resume
news.body: The U.S. and Iran agreed to stand down after exchanging strikes near the Strait of Hormuz last weekend; Doha peace talks are set to resume Tuesday, though Tehran is insisting on overseeing all Hormuz traffic — a major sticking point for commercial shipping.

news.head: Dow hits all-time high with Alphabet debut
news.body: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record 52,182.74 on Monday (PRIOR CASH CLOSE), boosted by Alphabet's nearly 5% gain on its first day as a Dow component, replacing Verizon.

news.head: SpaceX joins Nasdaq-100 on July 7
news.body: SpaceX (SPCX) will be added to the Nasdaq-100 before the open on July 7; index-tracking funds will begin buying shares after the July 6 close, creating a structural demand wave into next week.

news.head: Nike Q4 earnings after today's close
news.body: Nike (NKE) reports fiscal Q4 2026 results tonight; analysts expect revenue down ~2% and EPS down ~5.7% year-over-year, with the market watching CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround commentary and China demand signals.

news.head: JOLTS & Consumer Confidence due today
news.body: May JOLTS job openings and the Conference Board Consumer Confidence index are both scheduled for today; the prior JOLTS reading was 7.6 million — near a one-year high — and a repeat would reinforce the Fed's hawkish hold posture.

news.head: Comcast spin-off announced
news.body: Comcast said it plans to spin off its NBCUniversal and Sky businesses into a separate publicly traded company via a tax-free transaction expected to complete in roughly one year.

news.head: Fed Chair Warsh speaks Wednesday in Portugal
news.body: Warsh addresses the ECB forum in Sintra on July 2 — his second public appearance since the June FOMC — with markets alert for any further signaling on the pace and timing of rate hikes.

implications: The 10-year Treasury yield (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 4.38%) is holding just below recent highs as easing oil prices dampen near-term inflation risk, but the Fed's removal of its easing bias and a core PCE of 3.4% mean duration is not yet a safe harbor — real rates stand at 2.16% with 10-year breakeven inflation at 2.22%.

The DXY dollar index (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 101.11) edged to ~101.2 overnight (OVERNIGHT LEVEL) — on track for a second straight monthly gain — supported by Fed rate-hike expectations; USD/JPY (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 161.91) is at a 3-year extreme, meaning the yen is extraordinarily weak against the dollar, raising intervention risk from Tokyo.

Gold (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: $4,030.50/oz) ticked to ~$4,039.50 in early trading (OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET LEVEL) — elevated at the 78th percentile of its 3-year range — holding firm despite real yields above 2%, which historically would pressure it; the persistence signals ongoing safe-haven demand tied to geopolitical uncertainty.

Crude oil: WTI (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: $70.42/bbl) and Brent (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: $73.64/bbl) remain calm at the low-40th percentile of their 3-year range; tanker flows through the Strait of Hormuz are recovering, capping further price upside and taking some pressure off inflation expectations.

Positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Nasdaq 100 futures (at the 4th percentile of 3 years) and Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile) — a contrarian floor suggesting squeeze risk if sentiment shifts; VIX futures specs are also at the 12th percentile. Meanwhile, copper speculators are extended long (95th percentile) — a contrarian warning for industrial metals. In FX, British Pound specs are at a 3-year low short — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian-bullish lean for sterling. In rates, 3M SOFR specs are at a 3-year low — a contrarian-bullish lean for front-end bonds. High-yield bond dealer inventory sits at the 89th percentile — specs are heavily positioned, a contrarian warning for credit spreads.

watch.head: JOLTS (today ~10am ET)
watch.body: A reading well above 7.6M would bolster the Fed's hawkish case and could push the 10-year yield back toward 4.45%+; a miss below 7M could stall the dollar and ease rate-hike pricing.

watch.head: Nike earnings (after close)
watch.body: Guidance on China and North America demand is the key read-through for consumer cyclicals; the stock is down ~33% year-to-date and trading near $41-42, well below the ~$59 analyst consensus target.

watch.head: Iran-Doha talks
watch.body: Any breakdown in Doha diplomacy or renewed Strait of Hormuz interdiction would spike oil prices rapidly and re-ignite the inflation trade, hitting bonds and growth stocks hardest.

watch.head: SpaceX (SPCX) index flows
watch.body: Passive funds begin accumulating SPCX after July 6 close for July 7 inclusion; watch for front-running in the name and potential displacement selling in lower-weight Nasdaq-100 constituents.

watch.head: Fed Chair Warsh Wednesday (Sintra)
watch.body: Any language hardening the September hike probability or signaling a faster pace of balance-sheet reduction could reprice both the short end and equities sharply.

watch.head: Friday bond market close
watch.body: The bond market closes Friday, July 3 for Independence Day, so Thursday's June nonfarm payrolls report (consensus ~172K) will trade into a one-sided book — liquidity will be thin and volatility elevated.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: PRIOR CASH CLOSE 4.38%; overnight the yield is drifting just below that level (~4.376%) as lower oil prices reduce near-term inflation risk, per pre-market data.
2-year Treasury yield: PRIOR CASH CLOSE 4.10%; the 2s-10s curve is +28 bps (normal-sloping), a modest green signal for bank margins but not yet a clear all-clear for the economic cycle.

Real (inflation-adjusted) 10-year rate stands at 2.16% — meaningfully restrictive — and the 10-year breakeven inflation rate is 2.22%, meaning the bond market sees inflation running only modestly above the Fed's 2% target even as core PCE printed 3.4%.

The Fed's term premium — the extra yield investors demand for holding long-dated bonds rather than rolling short-term bills — sits at 75 bps, reflecting elevated fiscal supply risk and policy uncertainty under Chair Warsh.
Markets are pricing three Fed rate hikes this year with a September start; the SOFR-OIS and FRA-OIS spreads (both at -1 bp) signal interbank funding stress is essentially zero — plumbing is clean.
M2 money supply is growing at 5.6% year-over-year while the Fed's balance sheet is up just 1.1% — monetary accommodation is fading at the margin.

The Treasury's cash balance (TGA) stands at $918.7 billion — a large government war chest that, when drawn down, injects liquidity into markets; watch for any debt-ceiling or spending dynamics that accelerate that drawdown.
sections.positioning: In rates, 3M SOFR speculators are at the 1st percentile of their 3-year positioning range — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor suggesting front-end rates could rally (yields fall) if economic data disappoints.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500: PRIOR CASH CLOSE 7,440.43 (+1.18% Monday); pre-market futures ~7,455 (OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET LEVEL), roughly flat-to-firmer heading into the final Q2 session.

Nasdaq Composite: PRIOR CASH CLOSE 25,820.14 (+2.07% Monday); NDX futures ~30,164 (OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET LEVEL) — the Nasdaq-100 is on track for a ~6% June loss despite Monday's bounce, meaning quarter-end rebalancing flows may persist.
Dow Jones: PRIOR CASH CLOSE 52,182.74 — a record all-time high — boosted by Alphabet's Dow debut (+4.96%) and Tesla's 8.45% Monday surge.

Breadth is moderate but not euphoric: 64.8% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 50-day average and 63.1% above their 200-day average, while for the Nasdaq-100 only 52.5% are above the 50-day — the index rally is still concentrated.

VIX (a measure of how much investors are paying for downside protection on stocks): PRIOR CASH CLOSE 17.65 — benign but not complacent; VXN (Nasdaq equivalent) at 29.37 reflects continued nervousness in tech options.
SKEW index at 144.5 signals that sophisticated options traders are still buying tail-risk protection — the market is rallying but the smart money is hedged.
Equity-credit correlation stands at 0.755 — stocks and credit spreads are moving tightly together, meaning any credit wobble (e.g., HY spread widening) would quickly hit equities.

The Shiller CAPE ratio (a long-run valuation measure comparing stock prices to 10-year average earnings) is at 41.4x — historically stretched — and the equity risk premium (the extra return stocks offer over bonds) is deeply negative at -2.05%, meaning bonds look more attractive than stocks on a pure yield basis.
Rocket Lab (+15.9%) announced it would acquire Iridium in an $8 billion deal on Monday; space-sector momentum remains a thematic undercurrent.
sections.positioning: Nasdaq 100 and Russell 2000 speculative futures positioning is at the 4th and 2nd percentile of 3-year ranges respectively — speculators have almost no bullish bets left in small-caps and tech futures, which historically creates squeeze risk: if the market moves higher, short-sellers must buy to cover, amplifying the move. VIX futures specs are also at the 12th percentile — contrarian-bullish for the market.

single_name.note: CarMax Inc. (Consumer Cyclical) — company insiders have been buying (2 insider rules fired), large off-exchange block buying detected, a burst of unusual options activity, and the stock is trading above its 200-day moving average; shorts are moderate at 4.4 days-to-cover with low borrow cost (0.40%), limiting squeeze risk, but the insider-plus-institutional signal stack is fresh as of June 29.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield vs. investment-grade credit spread (HY-IG): 283 bps — the gap between what risky borrowers and safe borrowers pay; not alarming but worth monitoring given the equity-credit correlation of 0.755.
Investment-grade option-adjusted spread (IG OAS): 77 bps — tight, suggesting corporate bond markets remain orderly and large companies can borrow without distress premium.
Commercial paper funding spread (CPFF): 18 bps — the extra cost for companies to borrow short-term cash is minimal, meaning no funding stress for corporate treasuries.

Bank credit growth is running at 6.3% year-over-year — healthy expansion — and bank lending standards (SLOOS) show only modest tightening for C&I loans (8.1% net tightening) and near-zero for commercial real estate (2%).

Bank reserves at the Fed stand at $2,951.4 billion — ample system liquidity; the overnight reverse repo facility (RRP, a place where money-market funds park cash at the Fed) is essentially empty at $3.5 billion, meaning excess cash has largely been redeployed into the economy and markets.
The financial conditions indices (ANFCI: -0.477, STLFSI: -0.96) both remain in accommodative territory (negative = easier than normal), a tailwind for risk assets despite the hawkish Fed pivot.
Four-week average jobless claims: 224K (as of Jun 20); weekly claims: 215K — labor market remains firm, supporting the Fed's ability to hike without triggering recession fears near-term.

single_name.note: Scorpio Tankers Inc. (Energy/Shipping) — company insiders have been buying (2 insider rules fired), large off-exchange block buying detected, a burst of unusual options activity, trading above its 200-day line, and shorts are moderate at 4.0 days-to-cover (0.29% borrow cost); directly levered to Strait of Hormuz normalization — if tanker flows recover further, earnings estimates move higher. Signal is fresh as of June 29.
